dossier.architecture: Full-width intake, vertically translating reversible shooter and separate chain hooks.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; underfloor cross-shafts package elevator drives.
subsystems.intake: Omni wheels and printed wedges center notes after experiments with other wheel types.
subsystems.transfer: Shooter aligns with intake for transfer, then retains the note for the selected destination.
subsystems.scoring: Top/bottom shooter on a rotating carriage; intake rollers gently release amp/trap notes.
subsystems.endgame: Linear hook slides hold the chain while the scoring carriage rises to trap height.
subsystems.controls: Two Limelights aim relative to tags; high fixed-pose defensive shot bypasses occluded tag aiming.

versions: Prototype options included side-wheel and windup launchers. Removed wheels in regions not contacting the note to reduce rotating mass.
dossier.analysis: The same reversible carriage handles several destinations, but requires careful alignment and sequencing. Their high defensive shot is an alternate operating mode, not evidence that every normal shot clears a defender.
limits: Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.

context_documents.title: 2024-1756 · Omni centering and reoriented transfer need defined staging states
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1756: Omni centering and reoriented transfer need defined staging states

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Omni wheels and printed wedges center the note while allowing lateral motion. The rotating shooter aligns with the intake to receive it; paired sensors detect travel and possession. The same moving assembly uses gentle roller release for amp/trap rather than a high-speed shot.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies lateral freedom as the reason for the omni contact choice. Sensor feedback reduces the driver’s need to see the note and helps avoid acquiring a second piece.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A roller can create useful forward traction while resisting necessary lateral centering. Omni contact addresses that conflict, but the wedges still establish the note’s final alignment. A moving transfer interface adds a temporal constraint: feeding must wait for receiving geometry, then stop at a verified state before reorientation. Gentler release for a confined goal is a separate control mode from speaker firing.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test diagonal entries and sensor disagreement; measure capture/transfer tolerances at the rotating interface and retention during the following motion.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/Vnbv20qEBwQ](https://youtu.be/Vnbv20qEBwQ)

source_reviews.title: Argos 2024 robot software documentation
source_reviews.locator: Key Features, Commissioning, Controls and Software Checkout
facts: Carriage homing uses a horizontal note path with flywheels away from the intake. Controls expose feed in both directions, multiple preset positions and trap reversal.
Checkout distinguishes partial pickup, reversal and full staging before flywheel entry. The documented climb sequence raises hooks, then lowers hooks, raises shooter and scores.
The robot reports intake and aiming states with LEDs and driver feedback.
source_reviews.limitations: Documentation describes intended commands and commissioning, without proving event deployment or measured scores.

source_reviews.title: Argos Behind the Bumpers
facts: The dossier describes omni wheels and wedges, a rotating shooter carriage on an elevator, underfloor cross shafts and separate linear hooks.
source_reviews.limitations: No new caption review. Hardware details are inherited.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Argos put pickup, launch and placement on a common note route with a shooter carriage that can change both height and angle. The public checkout instructions make the operating boundary clear. A fully staged note sits short of the flywheels until the system intentionally feeds it. The carriage then has to preserve that staging through motion. Endgame adds another sequence where hook state establishes the chassis pose before the scoring carriage rises.
piece_flow: The older dossier describes a full-width collector that uses omni contacts and wedges to center a note.
The team documents partial pickup and reversing back out as checkout cases. The note is staged without entering the high-speed launch contact.

For speaker shots the shooter feeds forward into the flywheels. The manual controls also allow backward feed. The inherited dossier describes the carriage repositioning and using its slower intake-side contacts for amp/trap.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The intake is the front reference in the team instructions. At carriage zero, the note path is parallel to the floor and the flywheels face away from intake. That calibration links software commands to the physical handoff. The inherited account places elevator transmission under the floor and hooks on separate slides. Verify the passage through the pivot and carriage envelope with bumper, elevator and harness fitted.

subsystems.name: Pickup and staged feed
subsystems.construction: Inherited omni contacts and printed centering wedges. The team documentation confirms feed reversal and a fully staged position clear of the launch wheels.
subsystems.operation: Acquire, stage, reverse when needed and release on a separate command.
subsystems.team_rationale: The inherited dossier says the team arrived at the centering arrangement through experiments with wheel types.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An omni surface can permit crosswise translation while supplying forward traction. The wedges and rotating carriage still need a shared physical datum or the note may become trapped at the change of planes.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector exit, carriage entry and the position that separates storage from launch.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Run the team's partial, reverse and full-stage checks after work on any intake, sensor or carriage mount. Add worn-note tests at lateral offsets.
subsystems.unknowns: Sensor type and stop thresholds, roller speeds and exact clearances.

subsystems.name: Carriage, lift and hooks
subsystems.construction: The source documents a homed rotating carriage, elevator controls and hook commands. The older account describes independent lift and hook hardware.
subsystems.operation: Aim at a preset or move vertically for placement. Raise hooks during preparation, then lower hooks, raise shooter and score during the main sequence.
subsystems.team_rationale: The checkout explicitly divides climb preparation from loaded scoring.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A common tool buys multiple destinations at the cost of an additional axis and more states. The controls need a safe response if hook travel succeeds on only one side or carriage calibration shifts.
subsystems.interfaces: Carriage movement needs to avoid hooks, chain, frame and wiring. Floor zero should be a physical inspection feature after repairs.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Verify arm and elevator movement while carrying a note. Simulate a stalled hook and ensure it cannot trigger a bad placement.
subsystems.unknowns: Verified state-machine guards, loaded deflection, scoring heights and sequence timing.

subsystems.name: Controls and feedback
subsystems.construction: Public documentation lists forward/rear tag checks, aiming modes and different statuses for partial versus missing acquisition.
subsystems.operation: Provide distinct driver feedback and alternate aiming or preset paths.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team provides explicit commissioning and checkout steps for both acquisition and aim.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Distinguishing a partial from a missing note can determine whether the driver retries pickup or reverses the transfer. Preset shots help only if drivers know the allowed position and heading.
subsystems.interfaces: Pose estimate, aim state, carriage setpoints and feeder permission.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Induce vision loss and a half-captured note, then verify the operator gets an actionable status.
subsystems.unknowns: Tag filtering, shooting interlocks and pose error.

revisions: The corpus reports prototype launcher changes. The checked documentation distinguishes practice and competition software instances without dating mechanical revisions.
transferable_principles: Give staging a visible geometric reference and test incomplete pickup as its own state. Qualify each climb and scoring transition with the hardware it depends on.
disconfirming_conditions: A shared carriage becomes less attractive when elevator settling or recalibration slows the primary speaker cycle, or when a damaged note cannot reverse through its entry.
remaining_gaps: Source code for note sensing and climb interlocks, full interview, carriage/elevator drawing and event-specific settings.
